title: How a Nuclear Reactor Works in 60 Seconds ⚛️⚡ #shorts
description:
A fuel pellet smaller than your fingertip holds as much energy as a ton of coal. Inside a reactor, splitting uranium atoms heats water under high pressure, a steam generator makes steam, and a turbine and generator turn it into electricity. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#nuclearpower #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: The Secret
steps.text: One tiny *uranium pellet* makes as much energy as a whole ton of coal.

steps.label: Fission
steps.text: A neutron hits a uranium atom and it *splits*, releasing heat and more neutrons.

steps.label: Chain Reaction
steps.text: Those neutrons split more atoms. *Control rods* soak up neutrons to keep it steady.

steps.label: Hot Water
steps.text: The core heats water kept under *high pressure*, so it can't boil.

steps.label: Steam
steps.text: In the *steam generator*, that heat boils water in a second, separate loop.

steps.label: Electricity
steps.text: The steam spins a *turbine* and generator, then cools back into water.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Split atoms, make *steam*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
